title: Sync
summary: Peer-to-peer sync between the devices of one book, over the local network.
description: The author's phone and computers hold the same book. They sync directly with each other on the local network, without a server.

stories.as: an author who writes on more than one device
stories.want: the same book on each of them
stories.soThat: I can pick up wherever I left off

requirements.text: Two instances of the app on the same local network can sync their databases with each other.
Sync merges the changes each instance made since they last synced, instead of replacing one database with the other.

deprecation.reason: Sync follows Tally's design instead: change tracking in SQLite triggers and per-row conflict resolution by hybrid logical clock.

requirements.text: No book data passes through a server during sync.
Devices find each other by UDP broadcast and by probing each peer's last known address.
A discovery probe names the book by a short tag derived from its id, never by the id itself.
The channel between two devices is encrypted with the Noise protocol over TCP.
A peer is let in only when the key it proved in the handshake belongs to a device of the book.
A new device joins by scanning a pairing QR code, which works for one device and for `sync.pairing-lifetime`.
Every table syncs unless it is explicitly local to the device.
Concurrent changes to a row resolve to the version with the later hybrid logical clock.
Every device reaches the same rows whatever order changes arrive in.
Two rows that collide on a unique column keep the one with the lower id; the other is deleted on every device.
A note edited on two devices before they sync keeps both edits as revisions, so no edit is lost.
Settings that belong to one device (sync bookmarks, caches) are never synced.
A database restored from an older copy is detected at startup, or at its first sync if its marker was restored with it, and then takes a new device id and syncs from scratch.
On Android, sync also runs while the app is closed.
While the app runs, a desktop device keeps a daily copy of the database for `sync.snapshot-daily`, then one a week back to `sync.snapshot-weekly`.
Development and release builds never sync with each other.
